pageCache.text:
Welcome
A very warm welcome to Mount House, a co-educational, independent senior school for 11-18-year olds in leafy Hadley Wood, Hertfordshire.
Successful schools are about the personal development of each child as an individual. This includes their academic qualifications, but just as important is development of the skills of leadership, teamwork and collaboration, resilience and self-awareness which will allow them to enjoy success, happiness and fulfilment in their adult lives. In a changing world, Mount House students find a sense of purpose, where they are supported and encouraged to have an open mind and immerse themselves in school life.
Be You
Authenticity and Confidence
Mount House actively celebrates individuality, empowering students to embrace their unique identity and express themselves with courage and confidence. We pride ourselves on offering opportunities to all students. There is something for everyone and the supportive community gives them the platform to seize theirs, to develop their curiosity and unique talents through our rich academic and co-curricular programme.
Belong
Community and Compassion
Mount House is a unique community where every individual feels valued, supported, and connected – promoting kindness, inclusion, and compassion. Our small school setting intentionally develops the kindness and mutual respect that enables everyone to flourish.
Become
Aspiration and Growth
At Mount House, each student’s curiosity is nourished, encouraging them to strive for personal and academic success. It is our aim to unlock the individual and collective potential of all our students who are the leaders, entrepreneurs and game-changers of tomorrow. Our small school means that every student receives the personal attention and coaching that will enable their dreams to become reality.

pageCache.pageTitle: Head's Welcome | Sixth Form, North London | Mount House School
pageCache.text:
Head’s Welcome
A very warm welcome to Mount House, a co-educational, independent senior school for 11-18-year olds in leafy Hadley Wood, Hertfordshire.
I am delighted to introduce myself as Head of Mount House, and I feel incredibly privileged to lead this remarkable school community. At Mount House, we understand that true success comes from empowering each student to win their own race. This philosophy sits at the heart of everything we do. Whether a student excels in mathematics, finds their voice on the stage, discovers a passion for sport, or emerges as a natural leader, we celebrate and nurture their individual journey, and challenge them to develop across their skills and interests. We believe that when students are encouraged to be authentic, to embrace their unique strengths, and to pursue their personal best, they don’t just achieve, they thrive.
Our mission is simple: to be the school where curious and ambitious students flourish within a nurturing community. This is anchored by our core values that make Mount House a place to Be You, a place to Belong, and a place to Become.
In our small school environment, with a maximum of 350 students, we create the conditions where every young person can discover who they truly are. We celebrate authenticity and build confidence, ensuring that each student has the courage to express themselves and seize opportunities. Our rich and balanced academic and co-curricular programme ensures there truly is something for everyone. A place to Be You.
Mount House is fundamentally about community and compassion. Our intentionally small setting fosters the kindness and mutual respect that enables everyone to flourish. When students feel valued, supported, and genuinely connected, they develop the confidence to take risks, aim high, and support one another in their individual goals. A place to Belong.
We are committed to nourishing aspiration and growth in every student. Our dedicated staff provide the personal attention and coaching that transforms dreams into reality. We believe that high achievement is entirely possible without undue stress – when students are happy and feel safe, they naturally push boundaries and reach for their potential. Just take a look at our Sixth Former’s destinations! A place to Become.
As we look to the future, we remain focused on developing globally minded citizens who are optimistic problem solvers, young people who believe in both their own potential and their collective power to make a positive difference in the world. These are the leaders, entrepreneurs, and game-changers of tomorrow.
Mount House is a place of learning, discovery, laughter, and friendship – a place where students genuinely want to be. Small classes and tutor groups ensure that every individual receives the attention they deserve. I am honoured to lead Mount House into both the students’ and the school’s exciting future as we unlock the individual and collective potential of all our students. Thank you for considering Mount House School for your child. I hope you will find our website useful, and I very much look forward to meeting you in person and welcoming you to our school community.

pageCache.pageTitle: History of Mount House | Sixth Form, Barnet | Mount House School
pageCache.text:
History of Mount House
Mount House School is located in the Green Belt conservation area, with woodland and vast green spaces that the School can utilise for sports and outdoor teaching. The location is also on the eastern edge of the Battle of Barnet battlefield, a historic encounter in the Wars of the Roses in 1471. This provides an exciting link for the School to work closely with Barnet museum on local history projects.
The ‘Mount House’ itself is a stunning Grade II-listed fine red brick mansion with many notable architectural features such as the central doorway with Ionic columns and a six-panel door and cantilevered stair with two fluted balusters to each tread, and ramped handrail. Situated north of Hadley Common, on Camlet Way, Mount House sits to the northeast of a group of Grade II-listed 18th century houses clustered around the Grade II-listed parish church of St Mary the Virgin.
There is little available documentary evidence relating to the architect, original design, or early development of Mount House. Nevertheless, it is generally thought to have been built in the early 18th century, in a Palladian style, as an article in Country Life contended in 1942: ‘The original design must have been a perfect example of the smaller Georgian house and may well be due to such a scholar as Ware or Flitcroft.’ It was built on ground enclosed from Enfield Chase, and remained within Enfield parish until 1882.
As a family home, the most famous resident of ‘Mount House’ was Joseph Henry Green (1791-1863), an English surgeon who became the literary executor of Samuel Taylor Coleridge. Green lived at Mount House between 1836-1863 and was one of the most eminent surgeons in England at the time and also close friends of Samuel Taylor Coleridge from their first meeting in 1817. When Coleridge died in 1834, he made a huge tribute to their friendship by naming Green as the literary executor in his will, making him responsible for all his manuscripts, books and literary legacy. Green gave up his private practice at Lincoln’s Inn, and moved to Mount House where he lived for the rest of his life and wrote Spiritual Philosophy; founded on the teachings of the late Samuel Taylor Coleridge.
In wartime Britain, the educational role of Mount House began when it was commissioned as the home of the Architectural Association School between 1940-45. At the end of the war there was a renewed focus on education and the building was confirmed to retain its sole purpose of the education of children and was established as St Martha’s Senior School for girls (1947-2017).
The educational role of Mount House developed further as ownership transferred from the ‘Sisters of St Martha’ to the Mount House School Ltd and boys were welcomed as students in 2017. Mount House School became co-educational in all year groups in September 2022.

pageCache.pageTitle: ISI Reports | Sixth Form, Edgeware | Mount House School
pageCache.text:
Inspection Reports
Celebrating achievement at Mount House School
The ISI is appointed by the Department for Education to inspect association independent schools in England and an inspection is a rigorous process typically occurring once every three years.
The ISI introduced a new framework in September 2023. The material change in the new framework has been to abolish the ‘single word judgements’ so independent schools now either meet the standards, or not. The inspection report is structured around five key areas, wherein inspectors meticulously detail commendations for ‘Standards Met’ and provide insightful overviews, making recommendations for further improvement.
We are delighted that Mount House received the rating of ‘Standards Met’ across all five areas. This is a testament to the hard work and dedication of our remarkable team.
READ: ISI INSPECTION REPORT NOVEMBER 2023
Some highlights from the report are:
“The needs of individual pupils are central to the planning and delivery of the curriculum. The support offered to those with specific learning challenges is highly effective in ensuring they make progress in line with their peers.”
“The school provides effective programmes to develop the physical, mental and emotional wellbeing of its pupils.”
“Pupils have a clear understanding of the need for equality when considering others. They have developed platforms to discuss and review aspects of diversity and are successful at bringing about change. Opportunities for leadership and community involvement further support pupils’ personal development.”
“The school’s aim to support pupils to be intellectually curious, resilient and independent, and to become responsible for their own development, is at the heart of the many initiatives which leaders have embedded or, more recently, initiated.”
“The school’s values are clearly put into practice and reinforced throughout all aspects of school life. Leaders and directors demonstrate a willingness and desire to listen to pupils’ views and ideas.”
“Leaders have designed and implemented broad curricular and extra-curricular programmes, and enabled an individualised approach to pupils’ progress, which encourages pupils to engage in and enjoy their learning.”
“Heads of department communicate passion for their subjects, which further engages individual pupils’ intellectual curiosity and self- motivation and which impacts positively on the progress they make.”
“Leaders and teachers place a great emphasis on the individual needs of pupils”
“Leaders have provided a supportive and relaxing venue (the ‘Hive’) for pupils to take time out or to socialise with friends or engage in activities informally during free time. Pupils who have SEND are highly cognisant of the effect the support they receive has on their progress.”
“Pupils with English as an additional language (EAL) receive help with their written and spoken English, which helps pupils integrate into school life and supports their access to the curriculum. Leaders take care to support these pupils through a variety of initiatives including a buddy system and careful selection of GCSE choices.”
“The extra-curricular activities programme is both extensive and well attended. A wide range of academic, sporting, creative and performing arts opportunities plays a strong part in enriching pupils’ lives and develops in them an additional range of skills.”
“Leaders provide a curriculum, extra-curricular programme and social activities that enable pupils to develop high levels of respect, understanding and empathy through their experiences. They are supportive of each other and intolerant of any discrimination against any groups of pupils.”

Outreach
We believe that working closely with the local community is a vital part of being an independent school. Our students benefit from interactions with pupils at local primary schools and we’ve initiated several exciting projects in sport, music, literacy and classics.
A musical bond between Mount House School and Monken Hadley C of E Primary School was established in 2018, with Mr Whitehouse holding weekly workshops for pupils from years 4, 5 & 6. These fun packed, inclusive music rehearsals led to a great assembly performance at the end of the year. Since then, Monken Hadley pupils have been periodically invited to listen to whole-class musical performances at Mount House. These include Q & A time and a chance for Monken Hadley pupils to talk about their musical experiences.
World Book Day: Year 8 Librarians
On Wednesday 1st March 2023, librarians Fleur, Kasim, Florence, Thomas and Leo visited our neighbouring school, Monken Hadley Primary. The purpose of the visit was to talk about their duties as librarians and read to the children from their favourite childhood stories.
Leo reports: “As we arrived, we were greeted by the Head of school Mrs Eyres, who assigned us each a class to read to. I was fortunate to be chosen to read to the Year 1-2 class, Chestnuts. I read: ‘What the Ladybird Heard’ by Julia Donaldson which was a huge hit – thoroughly enjoyed by all.
“The children were very interactive, making noises for the different animals in the book, and asked many questions about being a librarian and what we do. It was fun to revisit a childhood favourite story and to share it with such an enthusiastic audience. As I left my class one little boy called out, “Hope to see you soon!” A sentiment shared by me and my fellow librarians.”
Students teach Classics at Hadley Wood Primary School
“In October 2022, Deni, Katherine, Philip, Thibaut, George and I went to Hadley Wood Primary School to teach a Year 5 class about the Olympian Greek gods, our first module in the Classical Civilisation GCSE course. We each created a slide on 2-3 of the gods, describing their features and responsibilities. After our PowerPoint we played three different games: bingo, creating top trump cards and a matching game.
It was so much fun (for us at least but I think the children enjoyed themselves!) – the children were particularly excited to receive house points when they won bingo! It was a good opportunity for us to consolidate our knowledge on the topic and develop our confidence to talk in front of people. I am thankful for this experience.” Written by Athena
Every year since 2022 we host a ‘Cricket Festival’ with local primary schools on Monken Hadley Common, the most recent being in June 2024. It is led by our PE department and some of our Mount House students. In the morning, there’s a carousel of drills and activities, followed by a tournament in the afternoon. The festival is always a great success to which pupils from both school look forward.
More news about our school outreach programme will be posted here soon.

Results & Destinations
Academic expectations are high and Mount House Sixth Form achieves excellent results. The vast majority of our leavers go on to study at their first choice university.
We are very proud of our value-added scores that show how we help our students achieve their potential as we have consistently scored in the top three for North London. Value Added scores show how much progress students who studied A-levels at Mount House made between the end of Key Stage 4 and the end of their A-level studies. The scores are calculated by comparing the A-level results of our students with the results of students in schools and colleges across England who started with similar results at the end of Key Stage 4.

Careers
Careers Education At Mount House School, we are committed to ensuring that every student is equipped with the knowledge, skills, experiences and confidence to make informed decisions about their future. Our careers programme provides a comprehensive, impartial and progressive framework that supports students from Year 7 through to Sixth Form, helping them explore the wide range of opportunities available to them, including university, apprenticeships, degree apprenticeships, employment, technical education routes and international pathways.
We believe that careers education should inspire ambition, broaden horizons, challenge stereotypes and help students understand how their learning connects to the world beyond school. Through curriculum learning, employer engagement, work experience, higher education guidance and personalised support, students are encouraged to develop the skills and aspirations required for successful futures. The Gatsby benchmarks provide a national framework to ensure excellence in careers education. During the 2025–26 academic year, Mount House achieved all eight Gatsby Benchmarks through a combination of Careers Awareness Week, employer encounters, work experience, university engagement, personal guidance interviews, curriculum integration and structured careers learning across year groups.
The careers programme is led by the School’s Careers Leader, Ms Ansari, and is supported by senior leaders, tutors, subject teachers, the Sixth Form team and external careers professionals. For careers enquiries from parents, students, employers, universities, colleges or training providers, please contact: Ms Kulsum Ansari (Head of Careers) Email: ansarik@mounthouse.org.uk

Higher Education & Careers
Mount House has a dedicated Careers professional offering individual support and guidance throughout the Sixth Form, working together with students to prepare them for work experience applications and internships. Practice interviews and coaching are offered to all students required to attend interviews for any application process.
Preparing for University Education at school is all about enabling students to take the next step – to attend their chosen university and pursue the career of their dreams.
The Head of Sixth Form and tutors support individual students throughout their application process as they choose a university, write compelling personal statements and prepare for interviews. We work closely with the prestigious Russell group of universities and Oxbridge colleges.
Our Head of Sixth Form has detailed knowledge to support arrangements relating to applications for American universities and leading universities throughout Europe. We also have expertise in the application process for Japanese Universities. Please click here to read more about this process and meet our Assistant Head, Mr Craig McCormick, who specialises in this area.
Intellectual discussion and debate are encouraged to increase student enthusiasm for their subjects. They will be introduced to new topics and the most up-to-date thinking in their proposed area of specialism to support their applications. Experienced tutors are on hand to support all university applications, whether it be Law at Imperial College London, Business Studies at Nottingham or Textiles at Loughborough.
Visits to Higher Education Fairs are arranged, and we work on a timetable of open events with leading universities. We also arrange visits and meetings with admissions tutors and lecturers from leading universities, and invite back former students to speak about their careers and studies.
Personalised Career Planning Year 10 students sit the Morrisby Profile Psychometric Test and feedback is provided by the Inspiring Futures Team at the start of Year 11, which is also followed up with individual interviews to explore possible career paths.
Work Placements and Practical Support The Careers Department holds an annual Careers Convention in the summer term where teachers, contacts from the world of business and willing parents help Year 10 and Sixth Form students with possible career choices. Upper Sixth students also receive a great deal of support with mock university interviews.
Our Head of Sixth Form runs a range of courses for the Sixth Form including:
Unifrog In keeping with our commitment to provide students with outstanding careers guidance and tailored university application support when choosing their next step after school, we are excited to inform you that our Unifrog platform is now live for Sixth Formers and Upper School.
Unifrog brings into one place every apprenticeship and university course in the UK, including every college at Oxford and Cambridge. This makes it easy for students to compare and choose the best university courses, apprenticeships or further education courses for them. They can also explore opportunities further afield by looking at English taught programmes in Europe in addition to the United States, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.
Unifrog can help students construct their Personal Statements, and for those applying in the United States, their Common Application essays. In addition, the platform allows students to investigate career opportunities, such as MOOCs and School Leaver Programmes. Unifrog makes it easy for students write their CVs and record their key skills and allows for teacher feedback.

pageCache.pageTitle: Celebrating the Class of 2026: A Level Results Day | Mount House School
pageCache.text:
Celebrating the Class of 2026: A Level Results Day
Posted: 13th August 2026
Today, we are pleased to celebrate the achievements of our Class of 2026 as they receive their A Level results and prepare to take the next steps in their journeys.
Results Day provides an opportunity not only to recognise their grades, but also the individual journeys behind them – the challenges overcome and aspirations realised.
Our 2026 results include 32% of grades at A*, A and B, and we are particularly pleased to see 100% A*-C grades in Computer Science and Criminology, while 75% of History grades were A*-B.
We are incredibly proud of the destinations our students are now moving on to, including Warwick, Bristol, Westminster, Nottingham and Leeds. Their chosen subjects are equally varied, including Physics, Computer Science, History, International Business and Creative Art. These destinations reflect the individual ambitions and interests of our students and the different pathways they have chosen to pursue.
As Head, Mr Cooper, said: “Behind every set of results is a unique young person with their own ambitions, challenges and achievements, and we are immensely proud of every member of our Sixth Form community. The individual attention, pastoral care and personalised support that sit at the heart of a Mount House education enable our students to flourish as individuals, developing the confidence and self-belief to pursue futures that are right for them.”
He added: “Whether our leavers are progressing to highly competitive universities, specialist courses, apprenticeships or other exciting opportunities, we take equal pride in helping each student find their own path. Their destinations may differ, but their journeys have all been characterised by determination, growth and a willingness to embrace opportunity, and we look forward to seeing all that they achieve in the years ahead.”
We would like to congratulate the Class of 2026 on their A Level results, we wish them every success as they begin this next chapter, and we look forward to seeing all that they go on to achieve.

Celebrating Our Best-Ever GCSE Results
Posted: 20th August 2026
Today, we are celebrating a fantastic set of GCSE results at Mount House School.
We are particularly proud of the individuals behind these headline figures. Eve achieved an incredible 10 grades at 8 or 9, while Reuben, Florence, Elin, Fred, Thomas, Annabel and Kasim all achieved eight or more grades at 8 or 9.
There were also outstanding results across a wide range of subjects, including 100% pass rates in Chemistry, Biology, Physics and English Literature, alongside excellent outcomes in Art, Geography and French.
As an all ability school, these results are particularly impressive and reflect what makes Mount House special: high expectations, personalised support and a genuine belief in every student’s potential.
A huge congratulations to all our Year 11 students, and thank you to our dedicated staff and supportive families for the important role they have played in supporting our students.
We look forward to seeing what our students achieve next, with many now progressing to our Sixth Form, where our newly transformed facilities will be ready to welcome them this September.

pageCache.pageTitle: Drama | Independent School, Hadley Wood | Mount House School
pageCache.text:
Drama
Drama at Mount House is an important aspect of school and there are many performance opportunities throughout the year, from House competitions to Shakespeare productions to large-scale musical theatre.
At Mount House there is the opportunity to study Drama at GCSE and A level, as well as through our co-curricular programme as part of the Drama Club.
We offer LAMDA lessons to all year groups as we recognise the benefit of drama and performance to young people, supported by experienced, enthusiastic staff with excellent facilities. We attend West End theatre productions to support and extend students’ knowledge and understanding of particular plays, acting and design styles, and production values in general.
All students have the opportunity to audition for a major production specifically targeted to their age group so that large roles are not just for the older students. Additionally, there are keenly contended House competitions where performance is a key element. Being involved in a production gives confidence-building skills and a sense of achievement within a creative team context.
Every year Mount House puts on a large-scale school musical production, which is the highlight of the year alongside other concerts and activities which are held.
She’s a member of the drama club and is doing GCSE drama and we’ve seen her confidence grow

pageCache.pageTitle: Music | Independent Sixth Form, Herts | Mount House School
pageCache.text:
Music
There are so many opportunities to come together for music-making at Mount House, with a programme of regular performances. We place a great emphasis on music in the chool and have a high uptake to our musical groups and work with them to develop those interests.
Singing is firmly embedded in the culture of the school. We have a school choir performing a range of sacred and secular vocal music including two- and three-part arrangements of classical and pop songs. The choir is coached by our specialist singing teachers and by our Head of Music and rehearse once a week.
In addition to choir we have ‘Open Mic’ events which allow performers to build their confidence in a friendly and environment. Students select songs and are accompanied by guitar or piano and learn to use microphones for vocal performance.
Our instrumental music clubs offer opportunities for students at all stages of their musical development from beginners to experienced performers.
We bring together a range of ensembles including:
House Band – an ensemble of experienced musicians who play at a range of school events
‘The Phantoms’– an inclusive and fun guitar group playing a range of classic rock music.;
Brass Group – year 7 brass programme. All year 7s gain the opportunity to learn brass instruments and form a brass ensemble group.
Drum Corps – learn rudimental drumming from technical point of view using drum kit and snare drum to become versatile and skilled.
Concert programme
From year 7 we have a structured programme to introduce students to musical performance starting with opportunities to play their instruments or sing at a school assembly. Our music curriculum covers all styles and skills needed in music.
Our spring concert in April showcases soloists and group instrumental performances.
Our Christmas concert in December is held in the local church, St Marys, and is a range of choral and instrumental performances of classic carols and more festive tunes.
Every year Mount House puts on an annual large-scale school musical production, which is the highlight of the year. ‘School of Rock’ musical was performed in Dec 2019 was a huge success as students relished the opportunity to perform and act to large audiences in a high-quality production.
A cappella competition
A group of students participate in the annual ISA A Cappella competition. If you’d like to join us, please come along to rehearsals on Wednesday lunchtimes.
Music lessons
We also offer a range of private music lessons for students where they can work towards the ABRSM Grades which can be arranged to host at School either at lunchtime or 4-5pm.
String instruments – violin, viola, cello, bass
Woodwind – flute, clarinet, oboe, saxophone
Guitar – acoustic, electric and bass
To find out more about our peripatetic music teachers, please click below:
Kindly return all completed music lesson forms to our Head of Music at whitehouses@mounthouse.org.uk
Music Technology
Our Head of Music is extremely experienced in all aspects of music technology. We use Sibelius and Logic X software with students to create their compositions. Students are also taught how to use mixers, amps and microphones safely for recording and performances.

pageCache.text:
Lunch
At Mount House we don’t just feed the brain, but satisfy students’ palates with deliciously appetising menus from award-winning caterers Thomas Franks Limited.
Lunches are freshly prepared on site so students can relax and choose from a healthy selection of hot and cold meals plus a salad bar, fresh fruit and desserts.
Our caterers promote healthy eating that strikes a balance between current eating trends and good nutrition, using fresh fruit and vegetables and organic meat and dairy products.
Their dedicated, imaginative team always welcomes students’ suggestions and regularly holds themed lunches.

pageCache.pageTitle: Mount House Communities | Sixth Form | Mount House School
pageCache.text:
Parent Teacher Association
Mount House Parent Teacher Association
The school has a Parent Teacher Association (PTA) where all parents, guardians and carers of current students, and school staff are also members.
The aim is of the PTA is to advance the education of students in the school in particular by:
The PTA contributes to the school community and offers another opportunity for any of its members to be involved in school life and support the school’s efforts. They organise a range of social opportunities for the Mount House family to come together and get to know each other over the course of the year. A variety of events have been held including a Summer Fair, Christmas Fair, Quiz Night, Bingo Night and more recently a Silent Auction.
Previously, a sponsored Moveathon was organised, which promoted the benefits of physical activity. Throughout the day, each year group participated in non-stop movement on the Multi Use Games Area with a personal trainer and the School Games staff. Students raised over £2,000, which was used to buy new outdoor tables to use in our beautiful school grounds. We are looking forward to running the event again in the new Michaelmas Term.
Funds were also raised for other items and activities such as new water fountains, an Easter event and Christmas and Summer Fair fun and games. All funds that are raised from events benefit the students and support the School objectives and is done through a process of consultation with the School and the PTA Committee.
The PTA also supports School functions such as open mornings, drama productions, Spring concerts and the annual sports day.
Contact for the PTA: MounthousePTA@mounthouse.org.uk
